episodes.title: Pupillary Reflex; Roadside to Resus
episodes.notes: We assess the pupils in almost every significantly unwell or injured patient - but how much are they really telling us? It is easy to document 'pupils equal and reactive' and move on, yet a changing pupil may be one of the earliest outward signs of a developing intracranial catastrophe. episodes.goal: Refine my pupil assessment so I can recognise early signs of rising intracranial pressure.

episodes.notes: Welcome back to September 2026's Papers of the Month, and this month we've got three papers that are really focused on the practical end of emergency and prehospital care. episodes.goal: Strengthen my sedation management after prehospital rapid sequence intubation so I can recognise and prevent under-sedation during transport.

episodes.notes: This month we've got another really varied mix of papers that all have the potential to influence everyday emergency and prehospital practice. episodes.goal: Weigh the impact of advanced critical care interventions on scene time when managing time-critical patients.

episodes.title: Laryngectomy and Tracheostomy Emergencies; Roadside to Resus
episodes.notes: Tracheostomy and laryngectomy emergencies are classic high-acuity, low-frequency situations. They do not happen every day, but when they do, airway problems can develop quickly, and the wrong intervention can make things significantly worse. In this episode, we work through the practical approach to these patients, starting with the most important distinction: a patient with a tracheostomy may…
episodes.goal: Strengthen my structured approach to airway emergencies in patients with a tracheostomy or laryngectomy.

episodes.notes: Welcome back to July's Papers of the Month. This month we've got three papers that tackle some of the biggest questions we face in emergency and critical care medicine. episodes.goal: Weigh the evidence on early vasopressors versus restrictive fluids so I can refine my management of septic shock.

episodes.title: Excellence in Facemask Ventilation; Roadside to Resus
episodes.notes: Face mask ventilation is one of those skills that can easily be overlooked. It's often seen as the simple bit of airway management — something that sits below the glamour of videolaryngoscopy, fibre-optics and endotracheal intubation. But the reality is that excellent face mask ventilation is one of the most important airway skills we have. In this episode, we take a deep dive into bag-valve-mask…
episodes.goal: Strengthen my bag-valve-mask ventilation technique so I can deliver effective ventilations and recognise when to move to another airway strategy.

episodes.title: June 2026; papers of the month
episodes.notes: This month's episode takes us deep into trauma care, but not just the medicine we deliver but also the systems, circumstances and social factors that shape who survives and who doesn't. episodes.goal: Strengthen my judgement on which prehospital trauma interventions offer the greatest benefit given how early most trauma deaths occur.

episodes.title: Reframing Anaphylaxis; Roadside to Resus
episodes.notes: Anaphylaxis is one of those conditions we think we have got pretty well sorted. Recognise it early, give adrenaline, support the airway and circulation, and crack on. episodes.goal: Recognise early respiratory compromise in paediatric anaphylaxis so I can escalate adrenaline and airway support before cardiovascular collapse.

episodes.title: May 2026; papers of the month
episodes.notes: This month's Papers of the Month is a real mix of papers that challenge some of the things we think we know, whilst also highlighting just how important systems and processes are in improving patient care. episodes.goal: Weigh the evidence on how aggressively to lower blood pressure in intracerebral haemorrhage before starting prehospital treatment.

episodes.title: Excellence in Defibrillation; Roadside to Resus
episodes.notes: Timely and effective defibrillation is fundamental to excellent outcomes in cardiac arrest care. But there is a growing body of evidence suggesting that how we deliver those shocks may matter just as much as when we deliver them. episodes.goal: Weigh the emerging evidence on vector change defibrillation and DSED so I can apply it appropriately in refractory VF arrests.

episodes.title: April 2026; papers of the month
episodes.notes: This month we're heading firmly into the prehospital and community space, looking at how we make decisions when the diagnostics are limited and the system around us is evolving. We start with a really practical question around traumatic pneumothorax. How good are we, clinically, at spotting the patients who actually need urgent decompression? episodes.goal: Update my understanding of early whole blood transfusion in major prehospital haemorrhage so I can support its use appropriately.

episodes.title: Decision Making; Roadside to Resus
episodes.notes: Decision making sounds like a slightly academic, niche topic… but in reality, it sits underneath every single thing we do in emergency and pre-hospital care. Every patient contact, every test we order, every treatment we start and every one we choose not to – is a decision made in an environment that is time critical, information-light and full of uncertainty. In this episode we take a step back…
episodes.goal: Strengthen my clinical decision making by weighing pre-test probability and test thresholds in uncertain prehospital presentations.

episodes.notes: March's Papers of the Month is here and we've got three absolute crackers to get stuck into. First up, we head prehospital to explore pseudo-pulseless electrical activity. episodes.goal: Recognise pseudo-pulseless electrical activity so I can treat profound shock rather than managing it as cardiac arrest.

episodes.title: Airway Management in Trauma; Roadside to Resus
episodes.notes: This episode is an absolute cracker! And we can say that as we've got outsider help... episodes.notes: Welcome back to February's Papers of the Month! We start this month looking a the right place to perform a prehospital anaesthetic. episodes.goal: Update my understanding of how the location and setup for prehospital anaesthesia influences patient safety and success.

episodes.title: Paediatric Seizures; Roadside to Resus
episodes.notes: Paediatric seizures are common, time-critical events and they're something most of us will deal with, whether that's pre-hospital, in the emergency department, or on the ward. episodes.goal: Strengthen my management of paediatric seizures by understanding why early benzodiazepine treatment matters before escalation.

episodes.goal: Strengthen my management of peri-intubation blood pressure to prevent secondary brain injury in severe traumatic brain injury.

episodes.title: November 2025; papers of the month

episodes.notes: Welcome back! In this episode, we're diving deep into something we all think we know, the Glasgow Coma Scale. episodes.notes: Welcome back to The Resus Room! This time, we're diving into the fascinating and often overlooked world of electrical injuries. episodes.goal: Refine my decision-making around resuscitative hysterotomy in maternal cardiac arrest, where early intervention may improve outcomes for both patients.

episodes.goal: Weigh the evidence for double sequential defibrillation in refractory ventricular fibrillation cardiac arrest.

episodes.title: Rhabdomyolysis
episodes.notes: Think of rhabdomyolysis and you'll think of an elevated creatine kinase (CK). The condition ranges from an asymptomatic period to a life-threatening condition with a hugely associated rise in CK which can also be accompanied by electrolyte disturbance, renal failure and disseminated intravascular coagulation. episodes.notes: Epistaxis is an extremely common presentation to both Prehospital Emergency Services and Emergency Departments. episodes.goal: Strengthen my management of epistaxis, from simple first-line measures through to controlling catastrophic haemorrhage.
